meta.name: Reliastra CLI — terminal design tokens
meta.status: proposal (design spike, not yet implemented in cli/cmd/reliastra)
consumed_by: design/cli/demo/reliastra-demo.py  (runnable ANSI proof in a real terminal)
cli/cmd/reliastra  (future: theme.go, one table, generated from this file)
meta.law: A token is a role, never a colour. Code says `verdict.down`; it never says `red`, and it never hard-codes a hex value. Every role resolves four ways: truecolor, 256, 16 and none.

metrics.note: cell_w_px is font_size_px * advance_em. The mock renderer places every run on that grid, so what the image shows is what a terminal can print.

canvas.selection.comment: selected row, active item in a prompt

line.hairline.comment: rules under headings, table header separator

text.primary.comment: values, verdicts, the command you typed

text.faint.comment: rules, tick marks, scaffolding. Never carries meaning alone.

brand.comment: identity + interaction: rails, links, selection marker, the command word

brand.bright.comment: hover/active, focus, interactive affordance on dark

verdict.down.comment: confirmed failure / verification did not hold

verdict.unknown.comment: no observation, field absent. Same ink as text.tertiary on purpose.

provenance.comment: RESERVED. Where a number came from: vantage point, methodology version, hash, signature state. Never decoration.

tints.comment: Chip backgrounds are a role colour blended over canvas.base. Blended at render time so light and dark stay in step; solid, never translucent, because a terminal paints whole cells.
tints.text_on_chip: role colour at full strength, except brand: text.inverse on brand
tints.track_note: the unfilled cells of a meter: text.faint at 20% toward the canvas — a trough, not a slab, on both themes

section.use: ruled section headings (ANSI: plain upper case, tracking is a mock-only nicety)

key.use: left column of a kv block, column headers

value.use: right column of a kv block, table cells

numeric.use: latency, scores, counts. Always right-aligned, always with its unit.

mono_raw.use: ids, hashes, urls, paths. Never truncated silently.

rhythm.wrap: prose wraps at max_prose_width_cols, hanging-indented to the value column
rhythm.truncation: an id or hash is wrapped to a second line, never elided. Only names and urls may take `…`.

glyphs.law: Twelve marks, no dingbats. Every glyph above is inside IBM Plex Mono — the brand font — and inside DejaVu Sans Mono, Menlo, Consolas, SF Mono and Cascadia Mono, which together are what a developer's terminal actually has. A mark a common font cannot draw is a mark we do not ship: a tofu box in a verification record is a credibility failure, not a style choice.
glyphs.verdict_pairing: Shape and colour are always paired — ✓ × ! · carry the state when colour is stripped (NO_COLOR, colour-blind readers, CI logs, greps).
glyphs.meter_note: meter_empty is the same block painted in text.faint, not a dither glyph: a segmented bar with two inks reads as an instrument, ░ reads as noise.

ascii_tier.when: the terminal is not UTF-8, or TERM is dumb/vt100

shell_prompt.comment: The mockups draw a realistic prompt so reviewers judge the output in situ. The CLI never prints it.

grid.value_col: keyWidth + gutter (aligned per block, not global)

breakpoints.name: wide
breakpoints.behaviour: full tables, sparkline column, provenance footer on one line

breakpoints.name: default
breakpoints.behaviour: drop the sparkline column, keep every field

breakpoints.name: compact
breakpoints.behaviour: tables become kv stacks; urls wrap to their own line

breakpoints.name: narrow
breakpoints.behaviour: one field per line, no rules wider than the terminal, no meter — the number alone

fidelity.comment: Three levels, one code path. The level is chosen once, at startup, and every component honours it.

levels.when: stdout is a TTY, TERM != dumb, NO_COLOR unset, --color != never, width >= 80
levels.renders: roles in truecolor, tint chips, meters, sparklines, ruled headings, hints
identical layout; every role resolved through its ansi256 column

levels.when: TERM is xterm/screen-256color-less, or the terminal reports 8/16 colours
levels.renders: identical layout; roles resolved through ansi16, chips become reverse video

levels.when: piped, redirected, NO_COLOR set, --color=never, TERM=dumb, or CI detected
levels.renders: no escapes at all. Structure is carried by glyphs and alignment: ●◐✖○, ─, ›, — and column position. This is today's CLI, unchanged.
the API's own shape, keys alphabetical, no chrome, no hints, no colour, ever

invariants: Removing colour must never remove meaning: every state also differs by glyph, position or word.
Nothing is painted on stderr that stdout did not already earn: errors are plain text with a leading glyph.
A tint chip is never the only carrier of a verdict. The word is printed next to it.
--quiet drops chrome (rules, headings, hints); it never drops a field.

motion.comment: Motion is a progress signal, never decoration. All of it is suppressed when stdout is not a TTY.

spinner.track: the sweep is a single block crossing a six-cell track: a caliper measuring, not a fidget spinner. Track cells are text.faint; the sweeping block is brand.bright.
spinner.rule: the verb says what is happening (probing, hashing, reading the record); elapsed time appears after 400 ms; the whole line is one \r-redrawn row
spinner.why_not_braille: ⠋⠼ are missing from IBM Plex Mono, JetBrains Mono and several shipped terminal fonts. A spinner the font cannot draw is a tofu box that blinks.

live.shape: status line redrawn at 1 Hz; scrollback is never rewritten
live.rule: no full-screen clear, no alternate screen buffer, so Ctrl+C leaves the transcript intact and the output stays scrollable and greppable

voice.comment: The terminal is the product's most literal surface. These rules come from the repo's own honesty contract, not from taste.
rules: A verdict is stated with its scope: 'DOWN' is always followed by where and when it was seen.
One observation point is one observation point. No layout may put a region label where a reader will take it for corroboration.
Attribution is a score with a methodology version beside it. It is never printed as a cause.
A field the API did not return is — , never 0, never 'unknown', never blank.
Every failure names the next command. An error without an exit is a support ticket.
Lower case prose, UPPER CASE only for section labels and verdict words. No exclamation marks, no emoji, no cheerleading.
The exit code is part of the message: the last line of an error names it.
